name: grilling-the-plan
description: A method for turning a vague ask into an executable plan that survives contact with reality, by attacking every claim in it — including your own — before anyone builds.
coreRule: Adversarial effort spent before building is worth many times the same effort spent after. Three phases produce no plan text at all. They are the highest-value phases.

precedenceLadder.note: your rules file — how work is run
live code, config, data — beats every document
written against a snapshot; assume drift

phases.name: Acknowledge, flag, stop
phases.summary: Restate the ask in your own words. Name what is missing. Flag what would change the plan's shape. Then stop.
phases.output: A paragraph and two or three flags.

phases.name: Inventory — count before you plan
phases.summary: Read-only workers enumerate what exists, partitioned by file ownership so none overlap. Cite file:line. Give counts. Freeze the result.

phases.name: Triage what recon dug up
phases.summary: Sort discovered defects into fix-during-work / needs-a-human-decision / out-of-scope. Never absorb a discovery silently.

phases.name: Grill the documents against the running system
phases.summary: Check every load-bearing claim against the top of the precedence ladder. Hunt for things asserted to exist that do not, staleness, cross-document contradiction, and unflagged assertions.
phases.output: A contradictions register. Expect it to resize the work.

phases.name: Shape first — diagram before prose
phases.summary: A one-screen typed dependency graph, approved before any task text. A wrong diagram costs a minute; the prose it authorises costs hours.

phases.name: Decompose into owned tasks
phases.summary: One folder per task, each a contract: persona, owned files, evidence already gathered, steps, a loop with a cap, evidence-based done, do-NOT list, output contract. Own by file, not by task.

phases.name: Extract recurring context into skills
phases.summary: When the same warning appears in five task files it belongs in a skill. Group by category of work. Carry scar tissue, not generic advice. Load before the first tool call.

phases.name: Design isolation, then find the collision
phases.summary: Separate workspaces are the easy half. List files many tasks want, give each one owner, have everyone else emit a fragment, add an integrator.
phases.output: Isolation model, contended-file table, integrator role.

phases.name: Choose the substrate by measurement
phases.summary: Time a real fan-out on each candidate. Record effective parallelism, not the advertised cap. Find what actually binds. Name what a limit governs before it shapes the plan.

phases.name: Verify the environment the plan assumes
phases.summary: Check that the world the plan describes exists: paths, repos, scripts, permissions, topology, credentials. A failed read is not proof of absence.
phases.output: Corrections to the plan, applied at source.

phases.name: Ship the door with the building
phases.summary: One entry point with a read order, a paste-ready kickoff prompt, persistent memory updated, a published status surface, and hand-off items you cannot do yourself.

scaling.verification: one adversarial pass on the risky task
adversarial pass after every build task

scaling.isolation: worktrees + waves + integrator per merge group
scaling.verification: two independent adversarial passes; second must not see the first
two passes per task, plus a completeness critic per track

neverScaleDown.why: grilling documents against the running system is the cheapest phase and catches the most expensive errors
the plan is itself a document, and documents drift — including the one you just wrote

principles.text: Declare precedence before you start. Say out loud when sources disagree.
Count before you plan. Numbers size work; impressions don't.
Shape before prose. Reject a diagram, not a chapter.
Own by file, not by task.
Contended files get one owner; everyone else emits a fragment.
Never certify your own work. Structural, not preference.
Every loop has a cap. Hitting it is a stop-and-report.
Measure constraints; never quote them. Name what a limit governs.
Recurring context becomes a skill, loaded first.
Escalate on decisions, not on findings.

inwardFacing.text: Grill your own artefact last and hardest.
inwardFacing.why: Your plan is a document. Documents drift.

inwardFacing.text: When challenged, verify before you defend.
inwardFacing.why: A challenge can be factually wrong and still be pointing at a real defect. Defending misses it; conceding fixes the wrong thing.

inwardFacing.text: State your own errors plainly and fix them at source.
inwardFacing.why: Capture the pattern, not the event — then search for the same wrong claim everywhere else.

antiPatterns.because: the restatement is where mismatched understanding surfaces

antiPatterns.dont: Plan from a spec without checking it
antiPatterns.because: specs describe intended systems as though built

antiPatterns.dont: Write task prose before the shape is approved
antiPatterns.because: you will rewrite all of it

antiPatterns.dont: Let one worker review its own output
Assign work by task when tasks share files
Treat a failed read as proof of absence
Log lessons in a growing incident file
antiPatterns.because: fix the document that was wrong

antiPatterns.dont: Turn a review finding into a stop-gate
Ship a plan with no entry point

outputs.FINDINGS.md: always — what it learned, cited, CONFIRMED vs SUSPECTED, ends with what I did not test
outputs.CHANGES.md: if it changed anything — three lines per file: did / why / risk
outputs.QUESTIONS.md: if blocked — one question per heading, each with a recommendation
